Hi Alex & Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I misunderstood.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Current search & recommendations pipeline has high latency for inference (~600-900ms per request) causing degraded UX on peak traffic.
- Costs on current hosted LLM endpoints are spiking with bursty traffic; need predictable unit economics.
- Security/compliance: must keep PII out of logs and validate audit logging for queries.

Primary goals for this POC (success metrics):
1) Latency: bring 95th percentile tail latency under 250ms for 512-token typical requests.
2) Cost: reduce per-1k-token cost by at least 30% vs current provider in similar load.
3) Quality: keep top-3 retrieval/recommendation relevance within ±2% of baseline (using your eval prompts).
4) Security: demonstrate end-to-end data isolation (VPC peering or dedicated network) and audit log access.

Scope (what we’ll run during the 6-week pilot):
- Deploy Redwood dedicated POC: one dedicated GPU pool (8–16GB GPUs depending on model choice).
- Model variants: 1) high-quality (base) model for evaluation, 2) quantized variant for cost testing.
- Workloads: search recommendations path + batch reranking job (sample 100k queries).
- Eval plan: use your prompt set (attached sample) + automated eval harness to measure relevance and latency.

Owners & roles:
- Redwood: Marissa (PoC lead, PM), Rishi (infra & ops), Neha (security/compliance contact).
- StellarTech: Alex (product), Priya (data/ML), procurement@stellartech.com (procurement).

High-level timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): Access & infra prep, sign MSA/POC SOW, exchange keys.
- Week 1: Model selection, baseline run, initial latency/cost measurements.
- Weeks 2–3: Prompt tuning & quantization experiments, run evals on prompt set.
- Week 4: Scale tests (peak traffic simulation), finalize metrics.
- Week 5–6: Wrap-up, run final regression tests, deliver findings and recommended configuration.

Access & setup steps we need from StellarTech:
1) Create a service account for Redwood with minimal permissions (details in attached doc).
2) Provision a test dataset snapshot (S3 link or temporary credentials) with ~100k sample queries.
3) Confirm network option: VPC peering or allowlisted IPs for the dedicated endpoint.
4) Provide your eval prompt set (we got a sample; a full set of ~500 prompts would be ideal).

Attachments I’ve included: redwood-poc-proposal.pdf (SOW summary), poc-kickoff-agenda.docx, prompt-set-sample.csv (short).

Next steps / asks for this week:
- Alex/Priya: confirm SSO/network preference (VPC peering vs allowlist) and procurement contact for SOW.
- Procurement: if okay, we’ll send the DocuSign POC SOW link for signature.

Thanks — I’ll book the kickoff slot once we confirm access & SOW sign.

Marissa
